newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-REFEREE SENDS OFF TWO AND SPARKS NEW ROW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REFEREE SENDS OFF TWO AND SPARKS NEW ROW.

text.p: English referee Paul Danson sparked off a new row over match officials on Saturday when he sent off two Sunderland players for relatively minor offences and reduced the match against Arsenal to a farce.
With Sunderland having had the best of the opening spell and the game being played in a sporting spirit, Danson booked Sunderland striker Paul Stewart for a deliberate handball.
In only the 15th minute, he then booked Sunderland defender Martin Scott for a hard tackle on Arsenal's Lee Dixon.
Six minutes later he booked Scott and sent him off for a late tackle on Dixon, which looked clumsy but not malicious.
Then he had a stand-up row with Sunderland manager Peter Reid and sent him out of the dugout.
With half-time still six minutes away, he booked Stewart for a second handball and sent him off.
The match was effectively over as a contest. Sunderland played with their remaining nine men back in defence for the rest of the game before losing 2-0 to two late goals.

Reid was furious and could hardly find words to describe his feelings. Police protected Danson's dressing room door and Sunderland's fans went away feeling they had lost as much to the referee as to Arsenal.
Reid, who admitted he called the referee "a disgrace" added: "All we want from decisions is a bit of common sense. I didn't see a bad tackle in the game.

"Will I try to apologise to him? I think I'll have a beer instead. That referee is off my Christmas card list for a start. But I have to apologise for my actions. I was out of order and completely unprofessional. But you get carried away in an emotional game.
"I have tried to go into the referee's room and talk to him but the police are guarding the door and won't let me in."
Arsenal's caretaker-manager Pat Rice, who hands over to new boss Arsene Wenger on Monday, said he had every sympathy for Reid and Stewart.
Rice said: "I told Peter I thought the game had been spoiled by his two guys being sent off.
"If Paul Stewart had been my player I would have been very disappointed to see him sent off for handball.
"It is a shame and I felt the referee could have allowed him a bit of leeway. He could have said, `Do that again and you are off,' instead of showing the red card."

It is not the first time this season Danson has been involved in controversy. He reported Coventry manager Ron Atkinson for his behaviour after Atkinson told him he had missed a clear handball offence before Chelsea scored a goal against Coventry at Stamford Bridge three weeks ago.
Atkinson has since been charged with bringing the game into disrepute.
Two years ago Danson sent off Alvin Martin, then playing for West Ham, but the English Football Association later decided he was wrong to do so after examining video evidence.
The match followed a plea from referee David Elleray, who sent off Everton's Duncan Ferguson last week, for the soccer public to show greater understanding of referees' problems.
The officials are following strict orders from the governing bodies to apply discipline but have attracted criticism that some referees are following the edicts too closely.

Elleray wrote in Saturday's Daily Express: "We are prepared to hold our hands up and say we were mistaken. The general feeling is that this has been a tough start to the season and if we are brutally honest, we've not always got it right."

Last week in London, at a UEFA Round Table panel, leading referee Serge Muhmenthaler of Switzerland claimed: "Referees rarely make mistakes because they only make decisions when they are 100 per cent sure of themselves.
"I also don't think we need any help from technology or two referees to officiate one half of the pitch each."
Two referees ? At the moment the game seems to be having enough trouble with just the one.
